# Letter of Jeremiah Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Letter of Jeremiah 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/LJR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** A copy of a letter which Jeremiah sent to-the ones being-led-away as captives into Babylon by-the king of-the Babylonians, to-give-message to them according as he-was-commanded by God.

**1:2** On-account-of the-sins which you-sinned before God, you-shall-be-led-away into Babylon as captives by Nebuchadnezzar king of-the Babylonians.

**1:3** Therefore, having-entered into Babylon, you-shall-be there many years and for a long time, even until seven generations; but after this I-will-lead you-out from there in-peace.

**1:4** And now you-shall-see in Babylon gods of-silver and of-gold and of-wood, being-carried upon shoulders, making-afraid the-nations.

**1:5** Take-care therefore that you yourselves become-not at-all like the-foreigners and be-taken-with-fear by them,

**1:6** when you-see the-crowd from-before them and from-behind worshiping them. But say in your-hearts, "To you it-is-fitting to-be-worshiped, O Lord."

**1:7** For my messenger is with you, and he himself is-seeking-out your-souls.

**1:8** For their tongue is-polished by the-craftsman, and they themselves are-overlaid with gold and with silver; yet they-are false and they-are-not-able to-speak.

**1:9** And as for a virgin who-loves adornment, taking gold and fashioning a crown upon the-head of them —

**1:10** so also the-priests take gold away from their gods and spend it upon themselves, and also give some of it to the-prostitutes on-the rooftop;

**1:11** and they-adorn them with garments as with a human being — these gods of-silver and gods of-gold and gods of-wood —

**1:12** though they-are-not-able to-save themselves from rust and from moth. But having-covered them with a purple garment,

**1:13** they-wipe their face because of the-dust of-the house, which is much upon them.

**1:14** And [a man] having authority like a governor holds a scepter as-though a man who-has-sinned in a city;

**1:15** but this one does-not-do-away-with the one sinning against him. He-has in his hand a sword and an axe; but himself he-does-not-deliver from war and from robbers.

**1:16** From this it-is-evident that they-are not gods; therefore do-not fear them.

**1:17** For just-as a vessel that a man uses is-made-useless, so also are their gods. When they-are-set up in the-houses, their eyes are full of dust from the-feet of the-ones-entering.

**1:18** And just-as the-courts are-fenced-in upon one-sinning against a king, as though condemned to-death, so also the-priests make-secure their doors with locks and bars, lest they-be-plundered by robbers.

**1:19** They-light lamps for them — more than for themselves, though they-are-not-able to-see even one;

**1:20** they-are indeed like one of-the beams of-the house; and it-is-said their hearts are-gnawed-away, while the-crawling-things from-the ground devour them and their garments, and they-perceive-not.

**1:21** Their faces are-blackened by the-smoke that-is in the-house.

**1:22** Upon their body and upon their head bats and swallows and birds fly, and likewise the-cats.

**1:23** From this you-shall-know that they-are not gods; therefore do-not fear them.

**1:24** As-for the gold which they-have for beauty — unless someone wipes away the-rust, they-will-not-shine, for not even when they-were being-molded did they-perceive [anything].

**1:25** Having-been-purchased at great price, there-is no breath in them.

**1:26** Having-no feet, they-are-carried upon shoulders, making-visible to-the people their-own dishonor. Are-ashamed then also the-ones-serving them?

**1:27** If it-falls to-the ground, it itself does-not-rise up; and if someone sets it upright, by itself it-will-not-stand; and as-to offerings they-are set before them as before dead people.

**1:28** The things sacrificed to them their priests sell and spend; likewise also their wives salt some of them, but to-the poor and to-the helpless they-give nothing.

**1:29** The unclean and the-menstruous woman touches their sacrifices; knowing therefore from these-things that they-are not gods, do-not fear them.

**1:30** For how-is-it right to-call them gods? Because women set-before the-gods of-silver and of-gold and of-wood.

**1:31** And in their temples the-priests sit, with their garments torn, with their heads and beards shaved, and with uncovered heads.

**1:32** And they-howl and cry-out before their gods, as some do at a funeral feast.

**1:33** The priests take-away the-garments of them and clothe their wives and their children.

**1:34** Whether one does-evil to them or good, they-are-not-able to-repay. They-are-not-able to-appoint a king or to-remove one.

**1:35** Likewise they-are-not-able neither to-give riches nor to-give money; if one vows a vow to them and does-not-keep [it], they-will-not-demand it.

**1:36** They-are-not-able to-rescue a man from death, nor to-deliver the-weak from the-mighty.

**1:37** To a blind man they-are-not-able to-restore sight; they-are-not-able to-rescue a man who-is in distress.

**1:38** They-will-not-have-mercy on the-widow; they-will-not-do-good to the-orphan.

**1:39** Their gods of-wood and of-stone and of-gold and of-silver are-like the-stones from-the mountain; the-ones-worshiping them will-be-put-to-shame.

**1:40** How then is it right to-think or to-say that they-are gods?

**1:41** Even the-Chaldeans themselves dishonor them, who, when they-hear of a mute one not-able to-speak, they-bring Bel and ask-him to-speak, as though he-were-able to-perceive.

**1:42** And they-themselves are-not-able to-understand and abandon them, for they-have-no perception.

**1:43** The women, having-girded-themselves with ropes, sit along the-roads burning bran-husks.

**1:44** And whenever one of them, having-been-drawn-away by some passer-by, lies with him, she-reproaches the one next-to her that she-was-not-counted-worthy as she herself was, nor was her rope broken.

**1:45** All-things done for them are false; how then is it right to-think or to-say that they-are gods?

**1:46** They-are-made by carpenters and by goldsmiths; they-will-be nothing other than what the-craftsmen wish them to-be.

**1:47** And the ones themselves who-made them — they-will-certainly-not-live for long; how then are-able the things-made by them to-be gods?

**1:48** For they-left falsehoods and reproach to-the ones-coming-after them.

**1:49** For when war or evil comes upon them, the-priests consider among-themselves where they-will-hide-themselves with them.

**1:50** How then is it-not-perceived that these-things are not gods, who-neither save themselves from war nor from evil?

**1:51** For since they-are wood, overlaid with gold and silver, it-will-be-known afterward that they-are false; to all nations and kings it-will-be made-manifest that they-are not gods, but works of men's hands, and no work of God is in them.

**1:52** Who then is it-made-clear to all that they-are not gods but works of men's hands, and no work of God is in them?

**1:53** They-are-not-able to-raise up a king over a land nor to-give rain to men.

**1:54** They-will-not-arbitrate a case nor will they-deliver a land from injustice, for they-have-no power, being as crows between heaven and earth.

**1:55** For even when fire falls upon the-house of these gods of-wood and of-silver and of-gold, their priests will-flee and will-escape, but they themselves will-be burned in-the middle like beams.

**1:56** And they-will-not-withstand a king and war. How then is it to-be-acknowledged or to-be-agreed that they-are gods?

**1:57** Gods of-wood and of-stone and of-gold and of-silver are-not-able to-save themselves from thieves and robbers.

**1:58** For those-who-are strong will-strip them of-the gold and the-silver and of-the garment which-is worn upon them and will-go-away, and they-will-not-be-able to-help themselves.

**1:59** Better therefore is a just king than a false god; likewise also a vessel in a house that is-useful to-the owner; it-is-better than false gods.

**1:60** Better also are the-doors of a house that-guard the things that-are in it than false gods; better also is the-wooden pillar of a palace.

**1:61** For the-sun and the-moon and the-stars, being bright and being-sent for necessities, are-obedient.

**1:62** Likewise also the-lightning when it-appears is visible; and the-same-way the-wind blows in every land.

**1:63** And the-clouds, when God orders them to-go over all the-earth, accomplish the-order; and the-fire being-sent-down from-above to-consume mountains and forests does what-is-commanded.

**1:64** But these-things are-not to-be-compared in appearance or in power to-one of them.

**1:65** From-which neither is to-be-thought nor is to-be-said that they-are gods, not being-able either to-judge-cases or to-do-good to men.

**1:66** Knowing therefore that they-are not gods, do-not fear them.

**1:67** For they-are-not-able to-curse kings, nor to-bless them.

**1:68** Signs in the-heaven they-do-not-show to-the nations, nor do they-shine like the-sun, nor give-light like the-moon.

**1:69** Animals are-better than they, which-are-able to-flee under cover and to-help themselves.

**1:70** Therefore it-is in-no-way clear to us that they-are gods; do-not fear them.

**1:71** For as a scarecrow in a cucumber-field guards nothing, so also are their gods of-wood and of-gold and of-silver.

**1:72** Likewise also their gods of-gold and of-silver and of-wood are-like a white-thorn in a garden, on which every bird sits; and likewise also to a dead body thrown into the-darkness.

**1:73** By the-purple and the-linen-cloth rotting upon them you-will-know that they-are not gods; and they-themselves will-finally-be-consumed and will-be a reproach in the-land.

**1:74** Better therefore is a just man who-has no idols; for he-will-be far from reproach.
